leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight members explicitly include targeted protein degradation in their round-1 configuration (Aili, Aqvist and Linke as a single part; Chabes as the second of two parts). Aili, Aqvist and Linke name the same trio, Crews, Deshaies and Handa, with Aqvist moving from Ciulli to Handa after the openings. Chabes names only Crews and Deshaies and would accept Handa as a third name only if the committee prefers a single achievement. Citation wording also differs: Aili and Linke tie PROTACs to the cereblon glue mechanism of thalidomide-class drugs, Aqvist uses chemically induced proximity from PROTACs to molecular glue degraders, and Chabes confines it to induced proximity with a ubiquitin ligase. Aili and Aqvist's other positions are not shared: Aili's alternatives are B051 and B019, Aqvist's are B020 and B037, Linke's are B068 and B019, and Chabes's are B032 and B037. All four acknowledge that no PROTAC drug is approved as far as they know. This count of four is below the five-vote majority.

Chabes alone proposes a two-part prize, base editing for David R. Liu alone and degradation for Crews and Deshaies, with the argument that both turn a biological outcome into a defined chemical event usable as a general tool. No other member lists B019 in a preferred configuration; Aili, Brzezinski and Linke hold it as an alternative, while Aqvist ranked it sixth and Somfai was critical. The sole-credit attribution to Liu is contested by Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke and Somfai.

Brzezinski prefers nitrogenase for Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt on the basis of structural confirmation over about three decades and a physically explicit mechanism. Zou and Chabes list B032 as an alternative. Their shared reservation, which Brzezinski himself concedes, is that the catalytic cycle (E4 state, substrate-binding site, order of proton and electron delivery) is not settled, and Zou also wants Dean's genetics and biosynthesis contribution weighed against Seefeldt.

Sparr prefers biomolecular phase separation for Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as a physical-chemical organizing principle of the cell. Linke ranked it fourth in the opening and proposed the same trio but did not carry it into his round-1 configuration. Aqvist, Brzezinski and Chabes question its maturity, and Sparr herself notes that it may not reach five votes.

Somfai prefers Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling for Buchwald and Hartwig, citing clean two-person attribution, mechanistic detail and decades of confirmation. No other member lists it as preferred or as an alternative in the round-1 files; the main objection raised by Somfai himself is overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize.

Zou prefers visible-light photoredox catalysis for MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson. Somfai lists B064 as an alternative. Zou concedes that MacMillan's 2021 organocatalysis prize is the weakest point and offers Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz or Konig as a fallback, while Konig, Nicewicz, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi retain real priority claims.

areas_of_agreement: Targeted protein degradation is the most widely supported candidate: it appears in the preferred configuration of four members and as an alternative for Brzezinski, Somfai, Sparr and Zou, so every member lists it somewhere in the round-1 files, either as preferred or as an alternative.
No member disputes the mechanistic validity of induced-proximity degradation; the open issues are clinical vindication, attribution and citation scope.
Several members state that no PROTAC drug is approved to their knowledge; none of the files verifies this independently, and it is treated here as an unverified claim.
Members consistently argue that the three-person cap forces omissions in every shortlisted field, and that attribution must follow the original discovery rather than laboratory seniority.
Car-Parrinello (B020) is acknowledged by several members as the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, but only Aqvist supports it and he does not carry it into his preferred configuration.
scientific_disputes: Whether degradation is one achievement or two: Aili, Aqvist, Chabes, Brzezinski, Somfai and Zou raise the question of whether PROTAC design and the cereblon molecular-glue mechanism are distinct achievements, while Aili and Linke argue for a single unifying citation on hijacking ubiquitin ligases.

Somfai asks what was new chemically in the cereblon discovery, which he describes as a target-identification result; Zou questions whether degrader-bound ternary-complex structures are numerous enough to support general design rules.

Whether base editing is chemically distinct from the Cas9 platform recognised in 2020: Chabes and Aqvist (in part) say yes because it replaces cleavage with a direct nucleobase reaction, while Aili, Aqvist, Somfai and Linke worry about overlap with the 2020 prize, and Somfai calls it protein engineering on an already rewarded platform.

Whether biomolecular phase separation is an established physical-chemical principle (Sparr) or still depends on which in-cell condensates are true equilibrium phases (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke).

Whether Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics (Aqvist's opening first choice) is a single chemistry achievement or a methods platform whose consequences lie in many fields, and how far the 2013 multiscale prize covers it (Brzezinski, Linke, Sparr).
attribution_disputes: Degradation, third laureate: Aili, Aqvist (after moving), Chabes (conditionally) and Linke name Handa; Zou's alternative keeps Crews and Handa in and weighs Ciulli against Deshaies; Aqvist's opening and Linke's opening included Ciulli. Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim are left out in every configuration and Chabes would omit Handa altogether.

Base editing: Chabes credits Liu alone, whereas Aili and Linke's earlier opening trio and Brzezinski's opening proposal include Komor and Gaudelli. Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke and Somfai note Kondo and Nishida's independent Target-AID priority, and Somfai and Chabes raise whether prime editing (B049) should travel with B019.

Nanopore sequencing (B068): Linke's opening trio was Branton, Deamer and Akeson, but Aili, Aqvist and Sparr point to unresolved priority among Deamer, Branton, Kasianowicz, Bayley and Akeson. Linke's own round-1 configuration does not include B068.
Nitrogenase: Brzezinski, Chabes and Zou's configurations differ on Seefeldt versus Dean, and Zou adds that Dean's genetics and biosynthesis contribution is not replaced by Seefeldt.
Photoredox: the early credit is spread among MacMillan, Yoon, Stephenson, Fukuzumi, Konig, Nicewicz and Melchiorre, and MacMillan's 2021 prize raises a repeat-recognition question (Somfai, Zou).
Lipid nanoparticles (B051): Aili and Sparr (opening) and Aqvist differ on Cullis, Anderson, Langer, Hope and Madden, and Aili raises MacLachlan's translation role and patent disputes.
maturity_disputes: Whether the lack of an approved PROTAC drug makes degradation premature this year: Aili, Aqvist, Chabes, Linke and Zou raise it, while Aili and Chabes argue that the mechanism is established regardless of approval.

Whether the nitrogenase mechanism is mature enough for a citation beyond the cofactor structure, given the unresolved E4 state, substrate-binding site and order of proton and electron delivery (Brzezinski, Chabes, Zou, Linke).
Whether phase separation is mature enough, given the unresolved physiological relevance of condensates (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke, Sparr's own admission).

Whether lipid nanoparticles (B051), with the strongest clinical validation cited in the files, are held as an alternative by Aili and Sparr only, and how much the 2023 Medicine prize overlaps with them.
Whether perovskite solar cells (B014) are ready, given unresolved stability, lead toxicity and scale-up, as noted by Linke, Somfai and Zou.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member reports a conflict requiring recusal. Aili notes a personal acquaintance with Sparr's work, which does not involve a shortlisted candidate; Aqvist notes a postdoc link to Warshel, who is not on the shortlist, and a field affinity with B020 as a computational chemist.

Brzezinski discloses scientific proximity to nitrogenase (B032) as a biochemist and a Stockholm University collegial tie to Zou, who has no credited candidate in his configuration; Zou discloses the same collegial tie to Brzezinski, who ranks B032 first.

Linke (chair) discloses that nanopore sensing (B068) and phase separation (B039) lie near his nanophysics interests, and notes the Lund affiliation shared with Somfai and Sparr; Somfai and Sparr likewise note the shared Lund affiliation and Sparr notes that her work on lipid self-assembly and amyloid is scientifically close to B039 and B051.
questions_for_round2: For B044, should the committee recognise PROTACs and molecular glues as one achievement or two, and if one, can a single citation state the unifying principle without implying that Handa's cereblon work is PROTAC chemistry?

Who should hold the third place beside Crews and Deshaies in B044, Handa or Ciulli, and does the committee support Chabes's Crews-and-Deshaies-only reading? What does Handa's work add mechanistically beyond target identification?
Does the committee treat the absence of an approved PROTAC drug as disqualifying this year, or is the established mechanism and the independent reproduction across many laboratories enough?

If a two-part prize is considered, is Chabes's pairing of B019 and B044 coherent, and can the committee agree on how base editing should be credited among Liu, Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida, and whether prime editing travels with it?
Which testable predictions of the phase-separation framework (B039) have been confirmed in living cells and not only in vitro, and does that satisfy the members who raised maturity concerns?

Can Brzezinski show that a nitrogenase citation can be framed on structure and cofactor function without crediting a mechanism the field has not settled, and who among Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt and Dean carries it?
Do the members who support B011, B064 or B032 see any configuration that could reach five votes, or should round 2 test the order between B044 and the single-supporter alternatives?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows one position with explicit multi-member support, degradation (B044, four of eight, below the five-vote majority), and one member (Chabes) pairing it with base editing. The other four members each prefer a different single ballot (B032, B039, B011, B064). Among the degradation supporters the open issues are citation scope, the third laureate and the clinical record, not the underlying science. As chair I include myself among the four supporters and note that my opening first choice, B068, did not attract other support and is not in my round-1 configuration.
